title: Counting each source window once removed a clear early antipodal earthquake excess in ComCat for 2000-2016
abstract: We tested whether an early excess of antipodal earthquake pairs extends across more source windows. We used the same ComCat snapshot and geometry as a prior campaign study. Sources have M7 or more. Targets have M5.5 or more and lie within 30 degrees of the antipode. Each before and after window spans three days. For 252 sources in 2000-2016, there were 112 after pairs and 50 before pairs. Only 45 after windows and 41 before windows had a target. A yearly common target-time shift test with 19,999 draws gave a one-sided p value of 0.3449 for the four-window excess. The pair count test gave p = 0.00675. Extra pairs beyond the first in each occupied window supplied 58 of the 62 excess pairs. In 2017-2025, occupied windows numbered 18 after and 26 before 114 sources. This test gives no clear increase in occupied source windows in either period. It does not exclude remote triggering or show that the two endpoints have equal power. Shared targets, source clusters, yearly phase assumptions, mixed magnitude types and the small sample limit inference. The package contains code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Observed occupied-window difference and yearly time-shift reference. Neither period has a clear positive excess.

citations.reason: The pair-count excess and its concentration motivate a new occupied-window endpoint. Same catalog and sample; this is not independent confirmation.
The study at 500-1500 km warns that sequence selection changes remote count estimates. The present geometry is antipodal.
